Release notes/v0.6.0/Oct 19, 2026

What's new in Cadence 0.6.0.

Cadence now learns how you decide and what you'd work on next, so your agents keep going while you're away. It guesses your answers before you give them, earns the right to give them itself, proposes the next task in each project with where the idea came from, runs it in its own worktree, and has the finished work waiting for your tap when you're back.

By Cadence Labs · Filed in Releases

§01 New

  • Your judgment. The scales button in the panel opens what Cadence has learned: the rules you've taught Claude in your memory notes and your own CLAUDE.md, and the corrections you make as you answer. Rules that only make agents more careful are kept on their own; anything that lets agents do more waits for your yes as an Inbox card. Learn from past sessions reads the Claude Code sessions you ran yourself, on this Mac only.
  • Cadence guesses before you answer. Every question an agent asks gets Cadence's guess first, and once you've answered, the card says whether it guessed the same. When it has earned it, its pick is outlined on the card and ⏎ takes it.
  • Hand over what it has earned. When Cadence has matched you often enough on a kind of question, it offers to answer those for you, with a countdown you can stop with Esc. It never answers anything that leaves your Mac or can't be undone, never picks "don't ask again", and one wrong answer drops it back a step.
  • What's next. Cadence drafts your goals for each project (change any of them) and proposes the next task it would start, quoting where the idea came from: your TODO files, something you said you'd come back to, or work left on a branch. One tap starts it in its own worktree, and it stops with commits on its branch. When an agent finishes, its card shows what Cadence would start next there: press N.
  • Finished work waits for you. Work Cadence started is checked against your rules before you see it, then waits in the Inbox. Ship it pushes its branch (merging stays yours); Set aside keeps the branch.
  • Your agents know your rules. Every Claude agent Cadence starts gets your rules and its project's goal, wherever it works. You can turn this off in Your judgment.
  • Step away. The moon button, or telling Talk "I'm stepping away", shows the day plan: what Cadence will start, what it answers for you, and how quiet your phone stays. When you're back, the briefing leads with what got done.
  • Take it with you. Export your judgment as an AGENTS.md with your rules and goals, or import a teammate's rules; each one waits for your yes.

§02 Changed

  • Your phone stays quiet while you're away: one push only when every agent is waiting on you, at most three a day.
